It is practically impossible to get an appointment by phone. I followed the online appointment process exactly, logging in at 8am on the dot, filling out the form straight away, fully aware it was likely a waste of time. Unsurprisingly, nothing came of it.

I then rang the surgery to explain that my condition was causing extreme discomfort, that it was most likely contagious and could be passed on to others in the community, and that I had arranged time away from work and my long daily commute to Cambridge specifically so I could make and attend an appointment. The receptionist repeatedly cut me off, spoke over me, and gave the same scripted responses, insisting I would definitely hear back with an appointment that day. Needless to say, I waited all day and heard nothing.

What this shows is simple: the GPs and staff at this practice have no genuine interest in helping the people who pay into and rely on this service. Hard-working, tax-paying members of society are left to suffer while the doctors and their staff make it as difficult as possible to be seen, as though the real aim is to avoid doing their jobs altogether.

I rarely go to the GP unless absolutely necessary, but on the occasions I have been seen the consultations have been rushed, dismissive, and carried out with no care or compassion. It is clear that patients are treated as a nuisance to be processed quickly and moved on, not as people in need of medical attention.

This surgery is an absolute disgrace. Sadly, it reflects a wider truth: GPs across the country appear more interested in protecting their salaries and reducing their hours than in fulfilling the most basic duty of care.
